title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 399
paragraphs: Such is the account given by the Persians; but as for the Egyptians, they claim Cambyses as one of their own, saying that he was born of this very daughter of Apries, for they say it was Cyrus who sent to Amasis for his daughter, not Cambyses. In saying this, however, they are not speaking correctly; nor can they have failed to notice — for the Egyptians are as well acquainted as any other people with the laws and customs of the Persians — first, that it is not their custom for a bastard to become king when there is a son born of a true marriage; and secondly, that Cambyses was the son of Cassandane, daughter of Pharnaspes, a man of the Achaimenid family, and not the son of the Egyptian woman. But they distort the truth of history, claiming kinship with the house of Cyrus. So much, then, for these matters.
